For \(\cos(2\pi y)\le 0\), we need
\[
y \pmod 1 \in \left[\frac14,\frac34\right].
\]
The conditions are periodic in \(x\) with period \(1\), so we search for the smallest positive \(x\).

We need, for \(k=0,1,2,3,4\),
\[
2^k x \pmod 1 \in \left[\frac14,\frac34\right].
\]

Start with \(k=0\):
\[
x\in \left[\frac14,\frac34\right].
\]

For \(k=1\), the smallest possible branch gives
\[
x\in \left[\frac14,\frac38\right].
\]

For \(k=2\):
\[
4x\in [1,1.5],\quad 4x\pmod 1=4x-1.
\]
Need \(4x-1\ge \frac14\), so
\[
x\ge \frac{5}{16}.
\]
Thus
\[
x\in \left[\frac{5}{16},\frac38\right].
\]

For \(k=3\):
\[
8x\in [2.5,3],\quad 8x\pmod 1=8x-2.
\]
Need \(8x-2\le \frac34\), so
\[
x\le \frac{11}{32}.
\]
Thus
\[
x\in \left[\frac{5}{16},\frac{11}{32}\right].
\]

For \(k=4\):
\[
16x\in [5,5.5],\quad 16x\pmod 1=16x-5.
\]
Need \(16x-5\ge \frac14\), so
\[
x\ge \frac{21}{64}.
\]
Thus the smallest possible value is
\[
x=\frac{21}{64}.
\]

Check:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x&\equiv \frac{21}{64},\\
2x&\equiv \frac{21}{32},\\
4x&\equiv \frac{5}{16},\\
8x&\equiv \frac{5}{8},\\
16x&\equiv \frac14,
\end{aligned}
\]
all lying in \([1/4,3/4]\), so all five cosines are nonpositive.

The answer is \(\frac{21}{64}\).
